script.text: Russia and Ukraine meet again tomorrow. Is anyone ready to give ground?

U.S. envoy Steve Witkoff says talks start Tuesday in Abu Dhabi and run two days. The agenda covers ending the war, security arrangements, de-escalation and humanitarian steps. Witkoff and Jared Kushner lead the U.S. side. Reports call it the first U.S.-mediated round since February.

The Kremlin says Vladimir Medinsky leads Russia's delegation. Deputy Foreign Minister Sergei Ryabkov joins for the first time, reports say. Ukraine's team is led by Rustem Umerov. France's foreign minister says European representatives will attend too.

Territory is the core dispute. In earlier rounds, Russia demanded that Ukraine leave the Donetsk region. Kyiv rejected that. Those rounds ended without a breakthrough, though the sides did swap prisoners. So far, neither side has announced any concession.
Will Russia and Ukraine agree to a ceasefire by year's end? Yes or no?

upload.title: Abu Dhabi Talks Start Tomorrow. Who Blinks First? #shorts
upload.description:
U.S. envoy Steve Witkoff announced that the United States will bring Russian and Ukrainian delegations together in Abu Dhabi on November 10 and 11. According to Witkoff, the agenda covers ending the war, post-war security arrangements, de-escalation and humanitarian measures; Witkoff and Jared Kushner lead the U.S. team. Reports describe it as the first U.S.-mediated round since February. The Kremlin has said Vladimir Medinsky will head Russia's delegation; according to reports, Deputy Foreign Minister Sergei Ryabkov joins the negotiations for the first time. Ukraine's delegation is reported to be led by Rustem Umerov. French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot said European representatives will take part in Abu Dhabi. Territory remains the central dispute: in earlier rounds Russia demanded that Ukraine withdraw from the Donetsk region, which Kyiv rejected. No concessions have been announced. Details could still change before the talks begin.
